summary: Adds a thumbnail helper that shells out to ImageMagick convert, a resize docs URL setting, and a GET /calc endpoint that evaluates an arithmetic expression from the query string.

findings.title: Remote code execution through eval of query parameter
findings.problem: The /calc handler passes req.query.expr straight to eval. Any caller controls the JavaScript that the server runs.
findings.consequence: Any client can run arbitrary code inside the Node process. That client can read secrets, touch the filesystem, or spawn processes.
findings.fix: Replace eval with a restricted arithmetic parser such as expr-eval or mathjs evaluate. Remove both suppression comments on these lines.

findings.title: Shell command injection through upload name
findings.problem: make_thumbnail interpolates upload_name into a shell string and runs it with shell=True. The docstring says upload_name comes from the upload form.
findings.consequence: An uploader can choose a name with shell metacharacters, such as a semicolon, and run arbitrary commands on the host. The same name can also contain path traversal to write outside THUMB_DIR.
findings.fix: Pass an argument list without shell=True. Reduce upload_name to a basename and reject names that start with a dash.

findings.title: Suppression comment hides the shell injection
findings.problem: The nosec B602 comment silences the warning for the shell=True call. That call really is injectable.
findings.consequence: Later scans stay quiet about a command injection that the code still contains.
findings.fix: Remove the nosec comment once the call uses an argument list without a shell.

findings.title: Lint suppression hides eval of request input
findings.problem: The eslint-disable-next-line no-eval comment silences the warning on the eval call. That eval runs request input.
findings.consequence: The linter never reports the remote code execution in the /calc handler.
findings.fix: Delete the disable comment when you replace eval with a safe expression parser.

findings.title: Pattern scan suppression hides eval of request input
findings.problem: The nosemgrep comment silences pattern scanning on the line that calls eval with req.query.expr.
findings.consequence: Future scans miss the remote code execution in the /calc handler.
findings.fix: Remove the nosemgrep comment together with the eval call.

findings.title: New behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: The change adds the /calc endpoint and make_thumbnail. No test in the repository exercises either one.
findings.consequence: Nothing would catch regressions in the endpoint or the helper, including hostile input.
findings.fix: Add tests for valid expressions, hostile expressions, and upload names that contain metacharacters.

dropped.reason: The noqa E501 comment only allows one long documentation URL constant. It hides no logic problem.
Importing subprocess is not a problem on its own. The real risk is the shell=True call raised separately.
